waters.read: 242 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Off 346 cfs a day ago and draining. Still a heavy-nymph river: a weighted stonefly or sculpin on the seams and undercut banks. One more day of this puts it near 200 cfs, which is wading water.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.0 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: At pool and easing, which holds fish on structure. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait across the wing dams and riprap, then the lock wall as it clears.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 27.8 ft and falling - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Down two-thirds of a foot on the day but still high and coloured. Fish the slack behind rock and the wall; a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the riprap.

waters.reading: Sound highs 4:55 AM at 3.0 ft and 5:40 PM at 3.9 ft at Hampstead; lows 11:12 AM at 0.5 ft and 12:07 AM (Mon) at 1.1 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 4:55 AM and 5:40 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Tide before lure. The fall off the dawn high runs to a half-foot low at 11:12 a.m. - that long ebb is the red drum window, the last of it on the grass edges and oyster bars with cut menhaden or finger mullet. A 77% waxing gibbous is building toward full, so spring tides are stiffening the inlet current. The Fisherman's Post monthly, published Aug. 3 and 20 days old, has whiting and black drum in the surf on shrimp and sand fleas, tarpon to 110 pounds off the Jolly Roger's king rigs, and specks, pompano and Spanish at Surf City pier. Flounder stays catch-and-release until Sept. 1.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature runs today - NOAA returned none.
